title: King in front wins
tagline: Two ranks of lead settles it — except one file

principles.prompt: Your king is two ranks in front of your pawn (not a rook pawn). What's the verdict?
principles.answer: Won, always — whoever moves. Two ranks of lead means you can always regain the opposition when it matters.

principles.prompt: Your king is one rank in front of the pawn. What's the verdict?
principles.answer: Won only if you have the opposition — or a spare pawn move to steal it. Without either, correct defence draws.

principles.prompt: Your king stands on the 6th rank, in front of the pawn. What's the verdict?
principles.answer: Won, full stop — no opposition needed. The 6th rank is past every defence.

principles.prompt: Which pawn breaks all the king-in-front rules?
principles.answer: The rook pawn. On the a- and h-files the defender only needs the corner, and Tier 1's fortress rules take over.

demos.title: Two ranks of lead
demos.intro: Black holds the opposition — and it doesn't matter. Two ranks of lead comes with the tools to steal it back.

steps.note: The spare tempo, spent at the perfect moment: kings faced, and now Black must move.
The king advances — two ranks ahead again, opposition in hand.
Black sidesteps, hoping to slip back in front.
Black scrambles for the queening square.
Opposition again, three ranks ahead of the pawn now.
The king owns e8. The pawn strolls e4, e5, e6, e7, e8 — nothing can touch it.

demos.title: One rank is not enough
demos.intro: Same idea, one rank less lead — and no spare tempo. Black has the opposition, and it holds forever.

steps.note: White sidesteps, looking for a way in.
Black mirrors. The face-off stays his.
The pawn advances — but it burns White's only flexibility.
One more push, king still beside the pawn, not in front.
— and Black takes the opposition. e7 will come with check, Ke8 blocks, and stalemate ends it. One rank of lead, no tempo: draw.

tests.title: Around the side
tests.intro: One rank of lead and no spare tempo — unless you act before he takes the face-off.

wrong.Kd5: Ke7 comes and bars d6, e6 and f6 together — with the face-off his, one rank of lead is only a draw.
wrong.Kf5: Ke7 comes and bars d6, e6 and f6 together — with the face-off his, one rank of lead is only a draw.

hints: If Black reaches e7 you'll never get past. Which square puts you two ranks ahead of the pawn right now?
Kf6 — outflank before the door shuts. From two ranks ahead the win plays itself.

tests.explanationAfter: Kf6 turned one rank of lead into two before Black could take the face-off. From there the pawn advanced with check, and Kf7 took the shield square — e6, e7, e8 can't be stopped.

tests.title: Face him or lose
tests.intro: His king leads the pawn by one rank. One rank is survivable — if you take the face-off right now.

wrong.Kd7: Kf6! — he outflanks to two ranks ahead of the pawn, and that's a won game. Meet him face to face instead.
wrong.Kf7: Kd6! — he outflanks to two ranks ahead of the pawn, and that's a won game. Meet him face to face instead.
wrong.Kd8: Too passive — Kf6 or Kd6 comes and his lead grows to two ranks: lost.
wrong.Kf8: Too passive — Kf6 or Kd6 comes and his lead grows to two ranks: lost.

hints: One rank of lead only wins with the opposition. Deny it to him.
Ke7 — face his king. He must move, the face-off is yours, and the straight-back defence holds.

tests.explanationAfter: With the face-off yours, his one rank of lead is worthless: mirror his sidesteps, drop straight back when the pawn advances, and Tier 1's stalemate finish waits at the end.

tests.title: Hold the line
tests.intro: Black's king leads his pawn by one rank, marching your way. Same rules, other direction.

wrong.Kd2: Kf3! — his king reaches two ranks ahead of the pawn on the open side, and the escort can't be stopped.
wrong.Kf2: Kd3! — his king reaches two ranks ahead of the pawn on the open side, and the escort can't be stopped.
wrong.Kd1: Too passive — his king steps two ranks ahead of the pawn and the verdict flips to lost.
wrong.Kf1: Too passive — his king steps two ranks ahead of the pawn and the verdict flips to lost.

hints: One rank of lead only wins with the opposition — so take the face-off from him.
Ke2 — meet him head on. He must move, and the mirror-dance holds the draw.

tests.explanationAfter: The rules are colour-blind: you faced his king, kept the face-off, and his single rank of lead buys nothing. Mirror every sidestep and drop straight back along the pawn's path.

tests.title: The exception
tests.intro: His king leads the pawn — the winning picture from this lesson. But it's a rook pawn.

wrong.Kd8: One square dawdled — Kb7 seals the corner and the pawn strolls home. The c-file zone won't wait.
wrong.Kd6: Wrong direction — Kb7 seals the corner behind you and the a-pawn walks in.
wrong.Ke7: Too slow — Kb7 comes and the door to c8 is shut for good.

hints: Against a rook pawn the verdict rules don't apply — Tier 1's corner fortress does. The sanctuary is the c-file, squares c7 and c8.
Kc8 or Kc7 — step into the drawing zone before Kb7 seals it.

tests.explanationAfter: On the a-file, king-in-front means nothing: once your king touches c8 or c7 he can never be evicted, and the pawn's escort has nowhere to stand. Always check the file before trusting the verdict.
